Fines went to a revolving fund outside the town budget, so the vote touches how magazines and databases are paid for; the board should say what covers them once fines stop, and a donation jar may be proposed as one source.

what_happened.line: Library trustees approved the February 18 minutes as amended after capitalization edits, then adjourned by roll call; no budget votes were taken.
The director said Lunenburg is moving to full CW MARS membership over several years, so the library's assessment will rise; an E-rate offset will partly cushion it.
Trustees spent a long stretch on reopening, browsing hours, curbside service and a staff vacancy; the director will ask the town manager about starting the search to fill it.
The strategic plan subcommittee reported that none of the consultant contract money has been spent, because the facilitator has not yet invoiced.
Trustees will read chapter two of the handbook before the next meeting, and bylaws work was added to the FY22 agenda.

why_it_matters: The CW MARS membership change is a rising library assessment that will show up in future library budget requests, which residents fund through the town budget, mostly taxes.
Reopening hours and curbside service decide when residents can use the building, and filling the vacancy bears on staffing for those hours.
watch_next: Trustees' next meeting: chapter two of the handbook to be read beforehand, with chapters one and two discussed.
The recarpeting bid request, which the architect is finalizing to go out through DPW.
